## Where can agents be used in infectious disease modelling? {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Many of the tasks often given to early career researchers
- Reading data. Pulling numbers out of reports, tables and figures
- Building infrastructure. Checks that rerun whenever the model or
  data change
- Optimising and differentiating model code
- Maths, such as analytical solutions
- Proposing candidate models and variations on them
- Managing complex experimental workflows
- Talking through model development. A rubber duck that answers back
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-workflow-agents.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The six-step workflow, question, data, model, fit, check and
report, with a tag over each. People over question; agents read and
digitise over data; people choose, agents write over model; agents,
every push over fit; agents run, people judge over check; agents draft,
people sign over report."}

![](figures/agents-rubber-duck.jpg){height="260px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="A yellow rubber duck sitting beside a computer keyboard."}

::: {.attribution}
After Abbott et al. 2025,
[A workflow for infectious disease modelling][wf] ·
BVDOutbreakSize [checks](https://github.com/epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml)
and [report](https://epiforecasts.io/BVDOutbreakSize/stable/) ·

## How we use agents to develop EpiNow2

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Our agents open pull requests as seabbs-bot and sbfnk-bot
- They fix bugs, simplify code, and add tests and benchmarks
- Review bots read each pull request first
- Then the other person reviews it, and a person merges
- 51 agent pull requests merged since March 2026

```{=html}
<div class="bots">
<div><img src="figures/seabbs-bot.jpg" alt="seabbs-bot avatar">
seabbs-bot</div>
<div><img src="figures/sbfnk-bot.jpg" alt="sbfnk-bot avatar">
sbfnk-bot</div>
</div>
```
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-agent-2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A specification or a conversation leads to agents writing the
tasks, which feed a loop of read, write, run and check. Passing code
becomes a pull request, which review agents send back into the loop and
we review. Merging refits the model and raises new tasks."}

::: {.attribution}
[EpiNow2](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2), GitHub API, 2 November
2026 · e.g. [#1523](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2/pull/1523),
[#1548](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2/pull/1548) and

## Empirical Research Assistance for epidemic forecasting

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
- An LLM-guided tree search writes and scores forecasting code
- It builds on existing domain expertise
- Many prompts describe models that hub teams already built
- A retrospective test claimed it beat the CDC ensemble
- Domain experts found that gain came from data revisions leaking into
  the test
- Run live in 2025/26, its ensemble ranked first for flu, COVID-19 and
  RSV
- My guess is few groups could run 207,500 candidate models
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](figures/agents-martinson2026-fig2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Inputs of a problem statement, data, libraries and evaluation
requirements feed a tree of candidate models, each node coloured by its
score, with the best leaf circled and the forecasting code it produced,
an SIR model fitted with scipy, shown as the output."}

::: {.attribution}
Aygün et al. 2026,
[Nature](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10658-6) ·
Bracher and Funk 2026,
[arXiv:2608.05883](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05883) ·
Martinson et al. 2026, Fig. 2,
[arXiv:2605.16238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16238)
:::

## Estimating the size of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
- Ebola disease in the DRC, built with agents
- We replicated the first published estimate the next day
- One model fitted to all the surveillance streams
- Estimates for each province and health zone
- Agents built the dashboard
- They built forecast evaluation, so forecasts are scored in real time
- They built the infrastructure to fit and check the model in public
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
![](figures/agents-bvd-dashboard.png){height="740px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="An interactive map of health zones in north-eastern DRC shaded by
current reproduction number, beside a national panel with a reproduction
number of 1.01 and weekly confirmed cases with a seven-day forecast.
Below, the reproduction number falling from about 2 in May to about 1
from August, and four small maps of health-zone estimates."}
